- **`examples`** (≥ 3; aim for 6): before the rule. Vary person, polarity, statement/question. `en` pins person and formality.

- **`smallPrint`**: the technical term, once ("Teachers call this…").

## 2. Work out what the reader knows on the chapter's day

**Session.** The days of all earlier units are counted, then this day's index (0-based) plus 1. For example, u01 has 10 days and u02 has 9, so u03 day 0 is session 20 and u03 day 4 is session 24. The gate works this out too (`chapterAt`), and that number is the one that counts.

**What the gate actually enforces**
- **legality**: every grammar node, pattern and graph lexeme the tagger finds in the text or in a gloss must be taught by this session, unless it falls inside a chunk that is already taught. **An unknown word that is in the graph cannot be glossed past this check.** Its gloss entry fails legality as well.

- **dupe**: a sentence, including its `Name:` label, that exactly matches any sentence in the corpus is an error, and that includes the bank. Running catchphrases have to vary: *¡De una!* → *Hernando y Simón: ¡De una!*
- **accent**: every `?` and `!` needs its `¿` and `¡`, **English lines too**. English lines must not contain questions or exclamations.

## 5. Coverage probe (save it in your scratchpad as `cov.ts`)

```ts
// npx tsx cov.ts <session> "<text>"   |   npx tsx cov.ts content/story/chNNN.json
import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { tagSentence, splitSentences, lemmatize } from '/Users/Matthew/Fluidez/app/src/engine/tagger';
import { loadCurriculum } from '/Users/Matthew/Fluidez/app/tools/gate/load';
const cur = loadCurriculum('/Users/Matthew/Fluidez/app');
let at: number, text: string, gloss: string[] = [];
if (process.argv[2].endsWith('.json')) {
  const c = JSON.parse(readFileSync(process.argv[2], 'utf8'));
  at = cur.chapterAt.get(c.id)!; text = c.text; gloss = c.gloss.map((g: any) => g.es.toLowerCase());
} else { at = Number(process.argv[2]); text = process.argv[3]; }
const glossed = new Set<string>();
for (const g of gloss) for (const w of g.split(/[^a-záéíóúñü]+/).filter(Boolean)) { glossed.add(w); const l = lemmatize(w); if (l) glossed.add(l.lemma); }
let words = 0, unk = 0, unG = 0;
for (const s of splitSentences(text)) {
  const r = tagSentence(s, cur.tagOpts);
  words += r.tokens.filter((w) => !w.punct && w.pos !== 'propn' && w.pos !== 'num').length;
  const spans = r.features.filter((x) => x.key.startsWith('chunk.') && (cur.taughtAt.get(x.node!) ?? 1e9) <= at).map((x) => x.span);
  const inChunk = (sp: [number, number]) => spans.some(([a, b]) => sp[0] >= a && sp[1] <= b);
  const out: string[] = [];
  for (const ft of r.features) {
    if (ft.node?.startsWith('l:')) {
      const t = cur.taughtAt.get(ft.node);
      if (t !== undefined && t <= at) continue;
      unk++; const g = glossed.has(ft.node.slice(2)) || glossed.has(ft.text.toLowerCase()); if (!g) unG++;
      out.push(`${ft.text}=${ft.node}@${t ?? '?'}${g ? '(gl)' : ''}`);
    } else if (ft.node && !ft.key.startsWith('chunk.')) {
      const t = cur.taughtAt.get(ft.node);
      if ((t === undefined || t > at) && !inChunk(ft.span) && cur.graphIds.has(ft.node)) out.push(`GRAM ${ft.node}@${t ?? '?'} "${ft.text}"`);
    }
  }
  console.log(s, out.length ? '\n    ' + out.join('  ') : '');
}
console.log(`session ${at}: words ${words}, unknown ${unk} (${(100 * unk / words).toFixed(1)}%), unglossed ${unG} (${(100 * unG / words).toFixed(1)}%)`);
```

How to read its output:
- `GRAM g:x@N` is a legality error. Rewrite the sentence.
- `word=l:x@N`, where N is greater than the session, is a legality error too, because the lexeme is in the graph. Replace the word.
- `word=l:x@?` means the word is not in the graph. It counts toward reading coverage, so gloss it or cut it.
- Paste a whole batch of candidate sentences at once to learn what a session allows before you draft.

## 2. Work out what the reader knows on the chapter's day

**Session.** The days of all earlier units are counted, then this day's index (0-based) plus 1. For example, u01 has 10 days and u02 has 9, so u03 day 0 is session 20 and u03 day 4 is session 24. The gate works this out too (`chapterAt`), and that number is the one that counts.

The reader knows:
- **Grammar and patterns**: every `focus` node on any day up to this session. If a node is scheduled in no unit, it is known from its graph `priority`.
- **Chunks**: every chunk up to this session, but **only as whole phrases**. If a sentence uses a chunk's words in a different way, the chunk does not cover them.
- **Words**: every lexeme whose unit day, or else `priority`, is ≤ the session. Function words (articles, pronouns, prepositions, *no*, *sí*, *y*, *pero*, *muy*, *mucho*, *gracias*…) all have priority 1. The grammar can still make them illegal, though. See the traps below.

**What the gate actually enforces**
- **legality**: every grammar node, pattern and graph lexeme the tagger finds in the text or in a gloss must be taught by this session, unless it falls inside a chunk that is already taught. **An unknown word that is in the graph cannot be glossed past this check.** Its gloss entry fails legality as well.
- **reading**: at most 2% of words unknown and unglossed, and at most 5% unknown in all. Names (tagged propn) and numerals are not counted as words. Words inside chunks still count: *Me llamo* is read as `l:llamarse` (session 72), *¿has estado?* as `l:estar`, *me gusta* as `l:gustar`.

- **Input days**: every new word of an Input day appears at least twice. Where a word cannot appear legally (for example *empezar* before stem-changing verbs are taught), drop it and say so in your report.
- **Dialogue first at A1**, written as `Name: line`. Use present-tense narration only once the present is taught. At A1–A2, keep short lines of English (Vale treating Tomás as a tourist, a word he blurts out) for comedy or plot, never to carry the Spanish.

  - a turn: something changes
  - a laugh, often Simón repeating a chunk at the worst moment
  - a small human moment
  - a thread back to the stakes (Altamira, the sale, the bet, Rosa's letter)

1. Plan each chapter in one line: the opening (new), the turn, the joke, the stakes, the hook.
2. Draft the text with the known-word list open beside you.

4. Write the JSON files. Then run the gate loop:
   ```
   cd /Users/Matthew/Fluidez/app && npm run gate -- --fix content/story/<your files>
   ```
   Fix every ERROR by rewriting the sentence. Never delete a check, a question or a sentence's meaning just to pass. Repeat until you get `gate: PASS — 0 error(s)`.
5. Run `npm run gate -- --strict content/story/<your files>` too. Low-confidence `tagger` errors from deliberate English lines or non-graph words such as *hostel* and *software* are acceptable. Fix anything else.

## 5. Coverage probe (save it in your scratchpad as `cov.ts`)

```ts
// npx tsx cov.ts <session> "<text>"   |   npx tsx cov.ts content/story/chNNN.json
import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { tagSentence, splitSentences, lemmatize } from '/Users/Matthew/Fluidez/app/src/engine/tagger';
import { loadCurriculum } from '/Users/Matthew/Fluidez/app/tools/gate/load';
const cur = loadCurriculum('/Users/Matthew/Fluidez/app');
let at: number, text: string, gloss: string[] = [];
if (process.argv[2].endsWith('.json')) {
  const c = JSON.parse(readFileSync(process.argv[2], 'utf8'));
  at = cur.chapterAt.get(c.id)!; text = c.text; gloss = c.gloss.map((g: any) => g.es.toLowerCase());
} else { at = Number(process.argv[2]); text = process.argv[3]; }
const glossed = new Set<string>();
for (const g of gloss) for (const w of g.split(/[^a-záéíóúñü]+/).filter(Boolean)) { glossed.add(w); const l = lemmatize(w); if (l) glossed.add(l.lemma); }
let words = 0, unk = 0, unG = 0;
for (const s of splitSentences(text)) {
  const r = tagSentence(s, cur.tagOpts);
  words += r.tokens.filter((w) => !w.punct && w.pos !== 'propn' && w.pos !== 'num').length;
  const spans = r.features.filter((x) => x.key.startsWith('chunk.') && (cur.taughtAt.get(x.node!) ?? 1e9) <= at).map((x) => x.span);
  const inChunk = (sp: [number, number]) => spans.some(([a, b]) => sp[0] >= a && sp[1] <= b);
  const out: string[] = [];
  for (const ft of r.features) {
    if (ft.node?.startsWith('l:')) {
      const t = cur.taughtAt.get(ft.node);
      if (t !== undefined && t <= at) continue;
      unk++; const g = glossed.has(ft.node.slice(2)) || glossed.has(ft.text.toLowerCase()); if (!g) unG++;
      out.push(`${ft.text}=${ft.node}@${t ?? '?'}${g ? '(gl)' : ''}`);
    } else if (ft.node && !ft.key.startsWith('chunk.')) {
      const t = cur.taughtAt.get(ft.node);
      if ((t === undefined || t > at) && !inChunk(ft.span) && cur.graphIds.has(ft.node)) out.push(`GRAM ${ft.node}@${t ?? '?'} "${ft.text}"`);
    }
  }
  console.log(s, out.length ? '\n    ' + out.join('  ') : '');
}
console.log(`session ${at}: words ${words}, unknown ${unk} (${(100 * unk / words).toFixed(1)}%), unglossed ${unG} (${(100 * unG / words).toFixed(1)}%)`);
```

How to read its output:
- `GRAM g:x@N` is a legality error. Rewrite the sentence.
- `word=l:x@N`, where N is greater than the session, is a legality error too, because the lexeme is in the graph. Replace the word.
- `word=l:x@?` means the word is not in the graph. It counts toward reading coverage, so gloss it or cut it.
- Paste a whole batch of candidate sentences at once to learn what a session allows before you draft.

End with a one-paragraph synopsis of the chapters.

## 2. What a script may use

A script's legality position is **the session on which its node is first in a day's `focus`**, and the node itself is allowed. ## 3. Anatomy (all required unless marked)

- **`hook`**: `line` = the human reason, in one or two plain sentences ("The first thing anyone in Bogotá will want to know is who you are…"); `es`/`en` = a line the learner would actually say, ideally from the story's world.
- **`examples`** (≥ 3; aim for 6): before the rule. Vary person, polarity, statement/question. `en` pins person and formality.
- **`rule`** (≤ 150 words, ~90 s reading): plain English, no jargon, built on the examples. Contrast with English and say what disappears or changes. Lists of forms are fine as short lines.
- **`smallPrint`**: the technical term, once ("Teachers call this…").
- **`soundTip`** (optional): only where a new sound matters. Describe it against English ("rhymes with *boy*", "like the *tt* in an American *better*"). Never assume audio.
- **`readAndPick`** (≥ 8): structured input. Spanish `es`, 2–3 English `options`, `answer` index. It must be **solvable only by noticing the form** (ending, article, mark, word order): options differ in exactly the thing being taught (*Somos de Cali* → we / they / I). Vary the position of the right answer.
- **`yourTurn`** (≥ 6): a ladder: **choose** (gap + two forms, type the whole sentence) → **type** (English prompt, Spanish answer) → **transform** (make it negative / plural / about *we* / polite). Each has `why`: one plain sentence, the reason in the learner's terms. `accept` lists real alternatives (word-order variants, *Me llamo* / *Soy*); every answer and accept must be typeable and legal.
- **`pitfalls`** (3–5): predicted English-speaker mistakes, `wrong` → `right` + `why` in one sentence ("Almost. *Es* tells you what something is…").
- **`personal`**: a closing prompt to say something true about yourself with the new form.

**Patterns** (`p:` nodes) are shorter but complete: 4–6 examples, a rule of ≤ 100 words, 8 readAndPick, 6–7 yourTurn, 3 pitfalls. Their readAndPick usually contrasts the pattern with what an English speaker would write (*Soy mesero* = a waiter vs *Soy el mesero* = the waiter).

## 1. Read first, in full

1. `tools/burn/brief.md`. These rules are binding.
2. `docs/unit-map.md`: the cast, the stakes and the story beat for every unit. Also look at the next two units, so you know where this week is heading.
3. `content/units/<unit>.json` for each unit: its `storyArc`, and for each day its `chapter`, `focus`, `chunks` and `lexemes`.

## 2. Work out what the reader knows on the chapter's day

**Session.** The days of all earlier units are counted, then this day's index (0-based) plus 1. For example, u01 has 10 days and u02 has 9, so u03 day 0 is session 20 and u03 day 4 is session 24. The gate works this out too (`chapterAt`), and that number is the one that counts.

The reader knows:
- **Grammar and patterns**: every `focus` node on any day up to this session. If a node is scheduled in no unit, it is known from its graph `priority`.
- **Chunks**: every chunk up to this session, but **only as whole phrases**. If a sentence uses a chunk's words in a different way, the chunk does not cover them.
- **Words**: every lexeme whose unit day, or else `priority`, is ≤ the session. Function words (articles, pronouns, prepositions, *no*, *sí*, *y*, *pero*, *muy*, *mucho*, *gracias*…) all have priority 1. The grammar can still make them illegal, though. See the traps below.

List the known nouns, verbs and adjectives before you write anything. Early on the list is tiny: at session 11 the reader does not know *hoy*, *casa*, *mañana*, *hora*, *abrir*, *mesa* or *carta*. Write the story with the words you have; don't write it first and translate it afterwards.

**What the gate actually enforces**
- **legality**: every grammar node, pattern and graph lexeme the tagger finds in the text or in a gloss must be taught by this session, unless it falls inside a chunk that is already taught. **An unknown word that is in the graph cannot be glossed past this check.** Its gloss entry fails legality as well.
- **reading**: at most 2% of words unknown and unglossed, and at most 5% unknown in all. Names (tagged propn) and numerals are not counted as words. Words inside chunks still count: *Me llamo* is read as `l:llamarse` (session 72), *¿has estado?* as `l:estar`, *me gusta* as `l:gustar`.
- So **you can only gloss words that are not in the graph** (*loro*, *pacto*, *tango*, *hostel*), or phrases that are legal anyway. A gloss is also a good way to give the meaning of a whole known-word phrase: `{"es": "Soy nieto de Rosa", "en": "I'm Rosa's grandson"}`.
- **dupe**: a sentence, including its `Name:` label, that exactly matches any sentence in the corpus is an error, and that includes the bank. Running catchphrases have to vary: *¡De una!* → *Hernando y Simón: ¡De una!*
- **accent**: every `?` and `!` needs its `¿` and `¡`, **English lines too**. English lines must not contain questions or exclamations.

**Known tagger traps (as of u01–u03)**
- At the start of a sentence, or straight after a `Name:` label, *Don* is read as `l:don`, *La* as an article and *Nombre* as a command. Put *Don Hernando* and *La Esquina de Rosa* mid-sentence.
- A one-word *¿Nombre?* or *¿Apellido?* is read as a verb. Use them in a full clause: *Tomás es nombre. Herrera es apellido.*
- *nada* can be read as *nadar*, *apuesta* as *apostar* and *silencio* as *silenciar*. Choose another word.
- Articles are illegal before session 6. So are possessives (*mi*, *su*) before 44, *muy* and *mucho* as quantifiers before 63, demonstratives (*este*, *esa*, *esto*) before 59, feminine adjective agreement (*contenta*, *colombiana*) before 40, question words outside chunks before 16, *por*/*para* before 164, *si* clauses before 154 and infinitive complements (*quiero comprar*) before 72.
- *¡Vamos!*, *vamos a + verb* and *hay que / tengo que + verb* may not match their chunks. Check them before you use them.
- English words the tagger treats as Spanish lexemes, such as *we*, *to*, *and*, *is* and *okay*, count as unknown words.

## 3. Shape and quality bar

- **Length**: A1 80–150 words, A2 150–250, B1 300–500, B2 500–700, C1 700–1,000. The first two chapters of the course are the exception: 40–90 words, mostly the chunks just met.
- **Input days**: every new word of an Input day appears at least twice. Where a word cannot appear legally (for example *empezar* before stem-changing verbs are taught), drop it and say so in your report.

## 5. Coverage probe (save it in your scratchpad as `cov.ts`)

```ts
// npx tsx cov.ts <session> "<text>"   |   npx tsx cov.ts content/story/chNNN.json
import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { tagSentence, splitSentences, lemmatize } from '/Users/Matthew/Fluidez/app/src/engine/tagger';
import { loadCurriculum } from '/Users/Matthew/Fluidez/app/tools/gate/load';
const cur = loadCurriculum('/Users/Matthew/Fluidez/app');
let at: number, text: string, gloss: string[] = [];
if (process.argv[2].endsWith('.json')) {
  const c = JSON.parse(readFileSync(process.argv[2], 'utf8'));
  at = cur.chapterAt.get(c.id)!; text = c.text; gloss = c.gloss.map((g: any) => g.es.toLowerCase());
} else { at = Number(process.argv[2]); text = process.argv[3]; }
const glossed = new Set<string>();
for (const g of gloss) for (const w of g.split(/[^a-záéíóúñü]+/).filter(Boolean)) { glossed.add(w); const l = lemmatize(w); if (l) glossed.add(l.lemma); }
let words = 0, unk = 0, unG = 0;
for (const s of splitSentences(text)) {
  const r = tagSentence(s, cur.tagOpts);
  words += r.tokens.filter((w) => !w.punct && w.pos !== 'propn' && w.pos !== 'num').length;
  const spans = r.features.filter((x) => x.key.startsWith('chunk.') && (cur.taughtAt.get(x.node!) ?? 1e9) <= at).map((x) => x.span);
  const inChunk = (sp: [number, number]) => spans.some(([a, b]) => sp[0] >= a && sp[1] <= b);
  const out: string[] = [];
  for (const ft of r.features) {
    if (ft.node?.startsWith('l:')) {
      const t = cur.taughtAt.get(ft.node);
      if (t !== undefined && t <= at) continue;
      unk++; const g = glossed.has(ft.node.slice(2)) || glossed.has(ft.text.toLowerCase()); if (!g) unG++;
      out.push(`${ft.text}=${ft.node}@${t ?? '?'}${g ? '(gl)' : ''}`);
    } else if (ft.node && !ft.key.startsWith('chunk.')) {
      const t = cur.taughtAt.get(ft.node);
      if ((t === undefined || t > at) && !inChunk(ft.span) && cur.graphIds.has(ft.node)) out.push(`GRAM ${ft.node}@${t ?? '?'} "${ft.text}"`);
    }
  }
  console.log(s, out.length ? '\n    ' + out.join('  ') : '');
}
console.log(`session ${at}: words ${words}, unknown ${unk} (${(100 * unk / words).toFixed(1)}%), unglossed ${unG} (${(100 * unG / words).toFixed(1)}%)`);
```

- `GRAM g:x@N` is a legality error. Rewrite the sentence.
- `word=l:x@N`, where N is greater than the session, is a legality error too, because the lexeme is in the graph. Replace the word.
- `word=l:x@?` means the word is not in the graph. It counts toward reading coverage, so gloss it or cut it.
- Paste a whole batch of candidate sentences at once to learn what a session allows before you draft.

## 2. Work out what the reader knows on the chapter's day

**Session.** The days of all earlier units are counted, then this day's index (0-based) plus 1. For example, u01 has 10 days and u02 has 9, so u03 day 0 is session 20 and u03 day 4 is session 24. The gate works this out too (`chapterAt`), and that number is the one that counts.

The reader knows:
- **Grammar and patterns**: every `focus` node on any day up to this session. If a node is scheduled in no unit, it is known from its graph `priority`.
- **Chunks**: every chunk up to this session, but **only as whole phrases**. If a sentence uses a chunk's words in a different way, the chunk does not cover them.
- **Words**: every lexeme whose unit day, or else `priority`, is ≤ the session. Function words (articles, pronouns, prepositions, *no*, *sí*, *y*, *pero*, *muy*, *mucho*, *gracias*…) all have priority 1. The grammar can still make them illegal, though. See the traps below.

List the known nouns, verbs and adjectives before you write anything. Early on the list is tiny: at session 11 the reader does not know *hoy*, *casa*, *mañana*, *hora*, *abrir*, *mesa* or *carta*. Write the story with the words you have; don't write it first and translate it afterwards.

**What the gate actually enforces**
- **legality**: every grammar node, pattern and graph lexeme the tagger finds in the text or in a gloss must be taught by this session, unless it falls inside a chunk that is already taught. **An unknown word that is in the graph cannot be glossed past this check.** Its gloss entry fails legality as well.
- **reading**: at most 2% of words unknown and unglossed, and at most 5% unknown in all. Names (tagged propn) and numerals are not counted as words. Words inside chunks still count: *Me llamo* is read as `l:llamarse` (session 72), *¿has estado?* as `l:estar`, *me gusta* as `l:gustar`.
- So **you can only gloss words that are not in the graph** (*loro*, *pacto*, *tango*, *hostel*), or phrases that are legal anyway. A gloss is also a good way to give the meaning of a whole known-word phrase: `{"es": "Soy nieto de Rosa", "en": "I'm Rosa's grandson"}`.
- **dupe**: a sentence, including its `Name:` label, that exactly matches any sentence in the corpus is an error, and that includes the bank. Running catchphrases have to vary: *¡De una!* → *Hernando y Simón: ¡De una!*
- **accent**: every `?` and `!` needs its `¿` and `¡`, **English lines too**. English lines must not contain questions or exclamations.

**Known tagger traps (as of u01–u03)**
- At the start of a sentence, or straight after a `Name:` label, *Don* is read as `l:don`, *La* as an article and *Nombre* as a command. Put *Don Hernando* and *La Esquina de Rosa* mid-sentence.
- A one-word *¿Nombre?* or *¿Apellido?* is read as a verb. Use them in a full clause: *Tomás es nombre. Herrera es apellido.*
- *nada* can be read as *nadar*, *apuesta* as *apostar* and *silencio* as *silenciar*. Choose another word.
- Articles are illegal before session 6. So are possessives (*mi*, *su*) before 44, *muy* and *mucho* as quantifiers before 63, demonstratives (*este*, *esa*, *esto*) before 59, feminine adjective agreement (*contenta*, *colombiana*) before 40, question words outside chunks before 16, *por*/*para* before 164, *si* clauses before 154 and infinitive complements (*quiero comprar*) before 72.
- *¡Vamos!*, *vamos a + verb* and *hay que / tengo que + verb* may not match their chunks. Check them before you use them.
- English words the tagger treats as Spanish lexemes, such as *we*, *to*, *and*, *is* and *okay*, count as unknown words.

```ts
// npx tsx cov.ts <session> "<text>"   |   npx tsx cov.ts content/story/chNNN.json
import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { tagSentence, splitSentences, lemmatize } from '/Users/Matthew/Fluidez/app/src/engine/tagger';
import { loadCurriculum } from '/Users/Matthew/Fluidez/app/tools/gate/load';
const cur = loadCurriculum('/Users/Matthew/Fluidez/app');
let at: number, text: string, gloss: string[] = [];
if (process.argv[2].endsWith('.json')) {
  const c = JSON.parse(readFileSync(process.argv[2], 'utf8'));
  at = cur.chapterAt.get(c.id)!; text = c.text; gloss = c.gloss.map((g: any) => g.es.toLowerCase());
} else { at = Number(process.argv[2]); text = process.argv[3]; }
const glossed = new Set<string>();
for (const g of gloss) for (const w of g.split(/[^a-záéíóúñü]+/).filter(Boolean)) { glossed.add(w); const l = lemmatize(w); if (l) glossed.add(l.lemma); }
let words = 0, unk = 0, unG = 0;
for (const s of splitSentences(text)) {
  const r = tagSentence(s, cur.tagOpts);
  words += r.tokens.filter((w) => !w.punct && w.pos !== 'propn' && w.pos !== 'num').length;
  const spans = r.features.filter((x) => x.key.startsWith('chunk.') && (cur.taughtAt.get(x.node!) ?? 1e9) <= at).map((x) => x.span);
  const inChunk = (sp: [number, number]) => spans.some(([a, b]) => sp[0] >= a && sp[1] <= b);
  const out: string[] = [];
  for (const ft of r.features) {
    if (ft.node?.startsWith('l:')) {
      const t = cur.taughtAt.get(ft.node);
      if (t !== undefined && t <= at) continue;
      unk++; const g = glossed.has(ft.node.slice(2)) || glossed.has(ft.text.toLowerCase()); if (!g) unG++;
      out.push(`${ft.text}=${ft.node}@${t ?? '?'}${g ? '(gl)' : ''}`);
    } else if (ft.node && !ft.key.startsWith('chunk.')) {
      const t = cur.taughtAt.get(ft.node);
      if ((t === undefined || t > at) && !inChunk(ft.span) && cur.graphIds.has(ft.node)) out.push(`GRAM ${ft.node}@${t ?? '?'} "${ft.text}"`);
    }
  }
  console.log(s, out.length ? '\n    ' + out.join('  ') : '');
}
console.log(`session ${at}: words ${words}, unknown ${unk} (${(100 * unk / words).toFixed(1)}%), unglossed ${unG} (${(100 * unG / words).toFixed(1)}%)`);
```

How to read its output:
- `GRAM g:x@N` is a legality error. Rewrite the sentence.
- `word=l:x@N`, where N is greater than the session, is a legality error too, because the lexeme is in the graph. Replace the word.
- `word=l:x@?` means the word is not in the graph. It counts toward reading coverage, so gloss it or cut it.
- Paste a whole batch of candidate sentences at once to learn what a session allows before you draft.

## What to check, and fix in place
- **Naturalness.** Would a Colombian say this? Fix stilted, calqued or textbook Spanish, and make sure the Spanish is neutral Latin American (no Spain-only words or forms).
- **Correctness.** Accents, agreement, mood, and clitic placement and order. Check that the English matches the Spanish exactly in person, number and formality.
- **Teaching quality.**
  - Hooks give a human reason to care.
  - Rules are in plain English, with no jargon, and ≤150 words.
  - Read-and-pick items really need the form noticed, not guessed from vocabulary.
  - Every your-turn `why` is a single plain reason.
  - Pitfalls are the mistakes English speakers actually make.
- **Sameness.** Rewrite runs of bank sentences that share a frame, opening or subject. Rewrite scenes or writing tasks that reuse a plot device or prompt from another unit. Never give the same thought twice.
- **Story continuity.** Chapters must pay off the previous hook, keep the characters' knowledge consistent and use no reused openings. They should be funny and give real stakes.
- **Answer fairness.**
  - `accept` lists cover the natural alternatives.
  - No gap has two valid answers unless every one is listed.
  - Scene `require` constraints don't reject good answers. Check each accept against its constraints (see `tools/burn/prompts/scenes.md` for the verifier).

- Edit only the files listed above. Keep ids stable: change text, never renumber. You may delete a bad bank sentence only if the bank stays at or above its count when you started.

- **Chunks gate as wholes.** A sentence inside a taught chunk requires the chunk, not the grammar it seeds; the chunk's `unpacks` node stays in `requires` and a taught chunk stands in for it. Write early content with the chunks the day has taught.

A script is the Introduce-day lesson for one node: the 10 minutes in which the learner meets it. The app is **text-only** (no audio), **no AI**, and the learner is an English-speaking adult.

## 1. Read first, in full

1. `tools/burn/brief.md` (binding: voice, LatAm Spanish, accents).
2. `content/units/u09.json` and the graph node for each script (`content/graph/grammar.json` / `patterns.json`): `title`, `es`, `en`, `note`, `contrasts`, `requires`, `sources`.
3. The node's `sources` in `/Users/Matthew/Fluidez/data/strand-lessons.js` (and `data/grammar.js`): mine examples, pitfalls, contrasts, the plain-English explanation. Convert Peninsular to LatAm.
4. `/Users/Matthew/Fluidez/docs/research/Structuring Spanish Learning for English-Speaking Adults.md`, section "Worked example lessons" (the Introduce-day timeline this anatomy comes from).
5. Earlier scripts in `content/scripts/` for the house style (u01's five are the reference).

## 2. What a script may use

A script's legality position is **the session on which its node is first in a day's `focus`**, and the node itself is allowed. So the u01 *ser* script (session 1) has no articles, no *-ar* verbs and about 130 words, mostly function words; the *-ar* script (session 8) has everything up to day 8. Chunks count only inside their matched span. Words not in the graph pass with a warning but the learner has not met them.

Probe every Spanish line first with the legality probe from `tools/burn/prompts/bank.md` §2, passing the session and the node: `… | npx tsx /tmp/fluidez-burn/scripts-u09-1/chk.ts <session> <node>`. The Spanish fields the gate checks: `hook.es`, `examples[].es`, `readAndPick[].es`, `yourTurn[].answer` and `accept`, `pitfalls[].right`. `pitfalls[].wrong` is deliberately wrong and never linted. English fields and `rule` are not linted, so the rule may quote Spanish freely — but keep it consistent with what the learner has seen.

## 3. Anatomy (all required unless marked)

- **`hook`**: `line` = the human reason, in one or two plain sentences ("The first thing anyone in Bogotá will want to know is who you are…"); `es`/`en` = a line the learner would actually say, ideally from the story's world.
- **`examples`** (≥ 3; aim for 6): before the rule. Vary person, polarity, statement/question. `en` pins person and formality.
- **`rule`** (≤ 150 words, ~90 s reading): plain English, no jargon, built on the examples. Contrast with English and say what disappears or changes. Lists of forms are fine as short lines.
- **`smallPrint`**: the technical term, once ("Teachers call this…").
- **`soundTip`** (optional): only where a new sound matters. Describe it against English ("rhymes with *boy*", "like the *tt* in an American *better*"). Never assume audio.
- **`readAndPick`** (≥ 8): structured input. Spanish `es`, 2–3 English `options`, `answer` index. It must be **solvable only by noticing the form** (ending, article, mark, word order): options differ in exactly the thing being taught (*Somos de Cali* → we / they / I). Vary the position of the right answer.
- **`yourTurn`** (≥ 6): a ladder: **choose** (gap + two forms, type the whole sentence) → **type** (English prompt, Spanish answer) → **transform** (make it negative / plural / about *we* / polite). Each has `why`: one plain sentence, the reason in the learner's terms. `accept` lists real alternatives (word-order variants, *Me llamo* / *Soy*); every answer and accept must be typeable and legal.
- **`pitfalls`** (3–5): predicted English-speaker mistakes, `wrong` → `right` + `why` in one sentence ("Almost. *Es* tells you what something is…").
- **`personal`**: a closing prompt to say something true about yourself with the new form.

**Patterns** (`p:` nodes) are shorter but complete: 4–6 examples, a rule of ≤ 100 words, 8 readAndPick, 6–7 yourTurn, 3 pitfalls. Their readAndPick usually contrasts the pattern with what an English speaker would write (*Soy mesero* = a waiter vs *Soy el mesero* = the waiter).

## 4. Quality bar

- Warm, brief, a little playful; a friendly peer. No exclamation-mark inflation.
- Every Spanish sentence is something a Bogotano would actually say. No sentence that exists only to show off a form.
- The learner can do every `yourTurn` from what the script showed. No trick questions.
- Prompts pin person, number and formality whenever the answer depends on it ("to a friend", "you all", "a woman speaking").
- When the vocabulary at that session is too thin for the node's own title (u01's *-ar* script before *hablar* was placed), use the verbs you have and say so in your report.

`cd /Users/Matthew/Fluidez/app && npm run gate -- --fix content/scripts/<file>.json …` until 0 errors. A warning that a script's node "is not scheduled in any unit" means you have the wrong node id. Fix legality by rewriting the Spanish, never by removing checks.

## 6. Report

Per script: counts (examples / readAndPick / yourTurn / pitfalls), anything you could not teach because of the session's vocabulary, and gate false positives as *exact sentence → finding*.

## 3. Anatomy (all required unless marked)

- **`hook`**: `line` = the human reason, in one or two plain sentences ("The first thing anyone in Bogotá will want to know is who you are…"); `es`/`en` = a line the learner would actually say, ideally from the story's world.
- **`examples`** (≥ 3; aim for 6): before the rule. Vary person, polarity, statement/question. `en` pins person and formality.
- **`rule`** (≤ 150 words, ~90 s reading): plain English, no jargon, built on the examples. Contrast with English and say what disappears or changes. Lists of forms are fine as short lines.
- **`smallPrint`**: the technical term, once ("Teachers call this…").
- **`soundTip`** (optional): only where a new sound matters. Describe it against English ("rhymes with *boy*", "like the *tt* in an American *better*"). Never assume audio.
- **`readAndPick`** (≥ 8): structured input. Spanish `es`, 2–3 English `options`, `answer` index. It must be **solvable only by noticing the form** (ending, article, mark, word order): options differ in exactly the thing being taught (*Somos de Cali* → we / they / I). Vary the position of the right answer.
- **`yourTurn`** (≥ 6): a ladder: **choose** (gap + two forms, type the whole sentence) → **type** (English prompt, Spanish answer) → **transform** (make it negative / plural / about *we* / polite). Each has `why`: one plain sentence, the reason in the learner's terms. `accept` lists real alternatives (word-order variants, *Me llamo* / *Soy*); every answer and accept must be typeable and legal.
- **`pitfalls`** (3–5): predicted English-speaker mistakes, `wrong` → `right` + `why` in one sentence ("Almost. *Es* tells you what something is…").
- **`personal`**: a closing prompt to say something true about yourself with the new form.

**Patterns** (`p:` nodes) are shorter but complete: 4–6 examples, a rule of ≤ 100 words, 8 readAndPick, 6–7 yourTurn, 3 pitfalls. Their readAndPick usually contrasts the pattern with what an English speaker would write (*Soy mesero* = a waiter vs *Soy el mesero* = the waiter).

## 1. Read first, in full

1. `tools/burn/brief.md`. These rules are binding.
2. `docs/unit-map.md`: the cast, the stakes and the story beat for every unit. Also look at the next two units, so you know where this week is heading.
3. `content/units/<unit>.json` for each unit: its `storyArc`, and for each day its `chapter`, `focus`, `chunks` and `lexemes`.

## 2. Work out what the reader knows on the chapter's day

**Session.** The days of all earlier units are counted, then this day's index (0-based) plus 1. For example, u01 has 10 days and u02 has 9, so u03 day 0 is session 20 and u03 day 4 is session 24. The gate works this out too (`chapterAt`), and that number is the one that counts.

The reader knows:
- **Grammar and patterns**: every `focus` node on any day up to this session. If a node is scheduled in no unit, it is known from its graph `priority`.
- **Chunks**: every chunk up to this session, but **only as whole phrases**. If a sentence uses a chunk's words in a different way, the chunk does not cover them.
- **Words**: every lexeme whose unit day, or else `priority`, is ≤ the session. Function words (articles, pronouns, prepositions, *no*, *sí*, *y*, *pero*, *muy*, *mucho*, *gracias*…) all have priority 1. The grammar can still make them illegal, though. See the traps below.

List the known nouns, verbs and adjectives before you write anything. Early on the list is tiny: at session 11 the reader does not know *hoy*, *casa*, *mañana*, *hora*, *abrir*, *mesa* or *carta*. Write the story with the words you have; don't write it first and translate it afterwards.

**What the gate actually enforces**
- **legality**: every grammar node, pattern and graph lexeme the tagger finds in the text or in a gloss must be taught by this session, unless it falls inside a chunk that is already taught. **An unknown word that is in the graph cannot be glossed past this check.** Its gloss entry fails legality as well.
- **reading**: at most 2% of words unknown and unglossed, and at most 5% unknown in all. Names (tagged propn) and numerals are not counted as words. Words inside chunks still count: *Me llamo* is read as `l:llamarse` (session 72), *¿has estado?* as `l:estar`, *me gusta* as `l:gustar`.
- So **you can only gloss words that are not in the graph** (*loro*, *pacto*, *tango*, *hostel*), or phrases that are legal anyway. A gloss is also a good way to give the meaning of a whole known-word phrase: `{"es": "Soy nieto de Rosa", "en": "I'm Rosa's grandson"}`.
- **dupe**: a sentence, including its `Name:` label, that exactly matches any sentence in the corpus is an error, and that includes the bank. Running catchphrases have to vary: *¡De una!* → *Hernando y Simón: ¡De una!*
- **accent**: every `?` and `!` needs its `¿` and `¡`, **English lines too**. English lines must not contain questions or exclamations.

**Known tagger traps (as of u01–u03)**
- At the start of a sentence, or straight after a `Name:` label, *Don* is read as `l:don`, *La* as an article and *Nombre* as a command. Put *Don Hernando* and *La Esquina de Rosa* mid-sentence.
- A one-word *¿Nombre?* or *¿Apellido?* is read as a verb. Use them in a full clause: *Tomás es nombre. Herrera es apellido.*
- *nada* can be read as *nadar*, *apuesta* as *apostar* and *silencio* as *silenciar*. Choose another word.
- Articles are illegal before session 6. So are possessives (*mi*, *su*) before 44, *muy* and *mucho* as quantifiers before 63, demonstratives (*este*, *esa*, *esto*) before 59, feminine adjective agreement (*contenta*, *colombiana*) before 40, question words outside chunks before 16, *por*/*para* before 164, *si* clauses before 154 and infinitive complements (*quiero comprar*) before 72.
- *¡Vamos!*, *vamos a + verb* and *hay que / tengo que + verb* may not match their chunks. Check them before you use them.
- English words the tagger treats as Spanish lexemes, such as *we*, *to*, *and*, *is* and *okay*, count as unknown words.

## 3. Shape and quality bar

- **Length**: A1 80–150 words, A2 150–250, B1 300–500, B2 500–700, C1 700–1,000. The first two chapters of the course are the exception: 40–90 words, mostly the chunks just met.
- **Input days**: every new word of an Input day appears at least twice. Where a word cannot appear legally (for example *empezar* before stem-changing verbs are taught), drop it and say so in your report.
- **Dialogue first at A1**, written as `Name: line`. Use present-tense narration only once the present is taught. At A1–A2, keep short lines of English (Vale treating Tomás as a tourist, a word he blurts out) for comedy or plot, never to carry the Spanish.
- **Every chapter has**:
  - a turn: something changes
  - a laugh, often Simón repeating a chunk at the worst moment
  - a small human moment
  - a thread back to the stakes (Altamira, the sale, the bet, Rosa's letter)
- **Pay off the previous hook in the first lines**, and end on a line that makes tomorrow matter.
- Follow the `storyArc`.
```ts
// npx tsx cov.ts <session> "<text>"   |   npx tsx cov.ts content/story/chNNN.json
import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { tagSentence, splitSentences, lemmatize } from '/Users/Matthew/Fluidez/app/src/engine/tagger';
import { loadCurriculum } from '/Users/Matthew/Fluidez/app/tools/gate/load';
const cur = loadCurriculum('/Users/Matthew/Fluidez/app');
let at: number, text: string, gloss: string[] = [];
if (process.argv[2].endsWith('.json')) {
  const c = JSON.parse(readFileSync(process.argv[2], 'utf8'));
  at = cur.chapterAt.get(c.id)!; text = c.text; gloss = c.gloss.map((g: any) => g.es.toLowerCase());
} else { at = Number(process.argv[2]); text = process.argv[3]; }
const glossed = new Set<string>();
for (const g of gloss) for (const w of g.split(/[^a-záéíóúñü]+/).filter(Boolean)) { glossed.add(w); const l = lemmatize(w); if (l) glossed.add(l.lemma); }
let words = 0, unk = 0, unG = 0;
for (const s of splitSentences(text)) {
  const r = tagSentence(s, cur.tagOpts);
  words += r.tokens.filter((w) => !w.punct && w.pos !== 'propn' && w.pos !== 'num').length;
  const spans = r.features.filter((x) => x.key.startsWith('chunk.') && (cur.taughtAt.get(x.node!) ?? 1e9) <= at).map((x) => x.span);
  const inChunk = (sp: [number, number]) => spans.some(([a, b]) => sp[0] >= a && sp[1] <= b);
  const out: string[] = [];
  for (const ft of r.features) {
    if (ft.node?.startsWith('l:')) {
      const t = cur.taughtAt.get(ft.node);
      if (t !== undefined && t <= at) continue;
      unk++; const g = glossed.has(ft.node.slice(2)) || glossed.has(ft.text.toLowerCase()); if (!g) unG++;
      out.push(`${ft.text}=${ft.node}@${t ?? '?'}${g ? '(gl)' : ''}`);
    } else if (ft.node && !ft.key.startsWith('chunk.')) {
      const t = cur.taughtAt.get(ft.node);
      if ((t === undefined || t > at) && !inChunk(ft.span) && cur.graphIds.has(ft.node)) out.push(`GRAM ${ft.node}@${t ?? '?'} "${ft.text}"`);
    }
  }
  console.log(s, out.length ? '\n    ' + out.join('  ') : '');
}
console.log(`session ${at}: words ${words}, unknown ${unk} (${(100 * unk / words).toFixed(1)}%), unglossed ${unG} (${(100 * unG / words).toFixed(1)}%)`);
```

- `word=l:x@?` means the word is not in the graph. It counts toward reading coverage, so gloss it or cut it.

## 1. Read first, in full

2. `docs/unit-map.md`: the cast, the stakes and the story beat for every unit. Also look at the next two units, so you know where this week is heading.

## 2. Work out what the reader knows on the chapter's day

**Session.** The days of all earlier units are counted, then this day's index (0-based) plus 1. For example, u01 has 10 days and u02 has 9, so u03 day 0 is session 20 and u03 day 4 is session 24. The gate works this out too (`chapterAt`), and that number is the one that counts.

The reader knows:
- **Grammar and patterns**: every `focus` node on any day up to this session. If a node is scheduled in no unit, it is known from its graph `priority`.
- **Chunks**: every chunk up to this session, but **only as whole phrases**. If a sentence uses a chunk's words in a different way, the chunk does not cover them.
- **Words**: every lexeme whose unit day, or else `priority`, is ≤ the session. Function words (articles, pronouns, prepositions, *no*, *sí*, *y*, *pero*, *muy*, *mucho*, *gracias*…) all have priority 1. The grammar can still make them illegal, though. See the traps below.

List the known nouns, verbs and adjectives before you write anything. Early on the list is tiny: at session 11 the reader does not know *hoy*, *casa*, *mañana*, *hora*, *abrir*, *mesa* or *carta*. Write the story with the words you have; don't write it first and translate it afterwards.

**What the gate actually enforces**
- **legality**: every grammar node, pattern and graph lexeme the tagger finds in the text or in a gloss must be taught by this session, unless it falls inside a chunk that is already taught. **An unknown word that is in the graph cannot be glossed past this check.** Its gloss entry fails legality as well.
- **reading**: at most 2% of words unknown and unglossed, and at most 5% unknown in all. Names (tagged propn) and numerals are not counted as words. Words inside chunks still count: *Me llamo* is read as `l:llamarse` (session 72), *¿has estado?* as `l:estar`, *me gusta* as `l:gustar`.
- So **you can only gloss words that are not in the graph** (*loro*, *pacto*, *tango*, *hostel*), or phrases that are legal anyway. A gloss is also a good way to give the meaning of a whole known-word phrase: `{"es": "Soy nieto de Rosa", "en": "I'm Rosa's grandson"}`.
- **dupe**: a sentence, including its `Name:` label, that exactly matches any sentence in the corpus is an error, and that includes the bank. Running catchphrases have to vary: *¡De una!* → *Hernando y Simón: ¡De una!*
- **accent**: every `?` and `!` needs its `¿` and `¡`, **English lines too**. English lines must not contain questions or exclamations.

**Known tagger traps (as of u01–u03)**
- At the start of a sentence, or straight after a `Name:` label, *Don* is read as `l:don`, *La* as an article and *Nombre* as a command. Put *Don Hernando* and *La Esquina de Rosa* mid-sentence.
- A one-word *¿Nombre?* or *¿Apellido?* is read as a verb. Use them in a full clause: *Tomás es nombre. Herrera es apellido.*
- *nada* can be read as *nadar*, *apuesta* as *apostar* and *silencio* as *silenciar*. Choose another word.
- Articles are illegal before session 6. So are possessives (*mi*, *su*) before 44, *muy* and *mucho* as quantifiers before 63, demonstratives (*este*, *esa*, *esto*) before 59, feminine adjective agreement (*contenta*, *colombiana*) before 40, question words outside chunks before 16, *por*/*para* before 164, *si* clauses before 154 and infinitive complements (*quiero comprar*) before 72.
- *¡Vamos!*, *vamos a + verb* and *hay que / tengo que + verb* may not match their chunks. Check them before you use them.
- English words the tagger treats as Spanish lexemes, such as *we*, *to*, *and*, *is* and *okay*, count as unknown words.

## 5. Coverage probe (save it in your scratchpad as `cov.ts`)

```ts
// npx tsx cov.ts <session> "<text>"   |   npx tsx cov.ts content/story/chNNN.json
import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { tagSentence, splitSentences, lemmatize } from '/Users/Matthew/Fluidez/app/src/engine/tagger';
import { loadCurriculum } from '/Users/Matthew/Fluidez/app/tools/gate/load';
const cur = loadCurriculum('/Users/Matthew/Fluidez/app');
let at: number, text: string, gloss: string[] = [];
if (process.argv[2].endsWith('.json')) {
  const c = JSON.parse(readFileSync(process.argv[2], 'utf8'));
  at = cur.chapterAt.get(c.id)!; text = c.text; gloss = c.gloss.map((g: any) => g.es.toLowerCase());
} else { at = Number(process.argv[2]); text = process.argv[3]; }
const glossed = new Set<string>();
for (const g of gloss) for (const w of g.split(/[^a-záéíóúñü]+/).filter(Boolean)) { glossed.add(w); const l = lemmatize(w); if (l) glossed.add(l.lemma); }
let words = 0, unk = 0, unG = 0;
for (const s of splitSentences(text)) {
  const r = tagSentence(s, cur.tagOpts);
  words += r.tokens.filter((w) => !w.punct && w.pos !== 'propn' && w.pos !== 'num').length;
  const spans = r.features.filter((x) => x.key.startsWith('chunk.') && (cur.taughtAt.get(x.node!) ?? 1e9) <= at).map((x) => x.span);
  const inChunk = (sp: [number, number]) => spans.some(([a, b]) => sp[0] >= a && sp[1] <= b);
  const out: string[] = [];
  for (const ft of r.features) {
    if (ft.node?.startsWith('l:')) {
      const t = cur.taughtAt.get(ft.node);
      if (t !== undefined && t <= at) continue;
      unk++; const g = glossed.has(ft.node.slice(2)) || glossed.has(ft.text.toLowerCase()); if (!g) unG++;
      out.push(`${ft.text}=${ft.node}@${t ?? '?'}${g ? '(gl)' : ''}`);
    } else if (ft.node && !ft.key.startsWith('chunk.')) {
      const t = cur.taughtAt.get(ft.node);
      if ((t === undefined || t > at) && !inChunk(ft.span) && cur.graphIds.has(ft.node)) out.push(`GRAM ${ft.node}@${t ?? '?'} "${ft.text}"`);
    }
  }
  console.log(s, out.length ? '\n    ' + out.join('  ') : '');
}
console.log(`session ${at}: words ${words}, unknown ${unk} (${(100 * unk / words).toFixed(1)}%), unglossed ${unG} (${(100 * unG / words).toFixed(1)}%)`);
```

How to read its output:
- `GRAM g:x@N` is a legality error. Rewrite the sentence.
- `word=l:x@N`, where N is greater than the session, is a legality error too, because the lexeme is in the graph. Replace the word.
- `word=l:x@?` means the word is not in the graph. It counts toward reading coverage, so gloss it or cut it.
- Paste a whole batch of candidate sentences at once to learn what a session allows before you draft.

You are the senior reviewer for unit `u10` of Fluidez. You are a Colombian-Spanish-fluent ELE teacher with a sharp editor's eye. Other writers drafted the unit's content, and it already passes the gate. Your job is to make it *good*: what a demanding learner and a native Bogotano would both respect.

## Read first, in full
1. `tools/burn/brief.md` (binding).
2. `content/units/u10.json` and `docs/unit-map.md` (this unit's place in the course and the story).
3. Every file of this unit:

## What to check, and fix in place
- **Naturalness.** Would a Colombian say this? Fix stilted, calqued or textbook Spanish, and make sure the Spanish is neutral Latin American (no Spain-only words or forms).
- **Correctness.** Accents, agreement, mood, and clitic placement and order. Check that the English matches the Spanish exactly in person, number and formality.
- **Teaching quality.**
  - Hooks give a human reason to care.
  - Rules are in plain English, with no jargon, and ≤150 words.
  - Read-and-pick items really need the form noticed, not guessed from vocabulary.

```ts
import { tagSentence, splitSentences, lemmatize } from '/Users/Matthew/Fluidez/app/src/engine/tagger';
import { loadCurriculum } from '/Users/Matthew/Fluidez/app/tools/gate/load';

} else { at = Number(process.argv[2]); text = process.argv[3]; }
const glossed = new Set<string>();

    } else if (ft.node && !ft.key.startsWith('chunk.')) {
      const t = cur.taughtAt.get(ft.node);
      if ((t === undefined || t > at) && !inChunk(ft.span) && cur.graphIds.has(ft.node)) out.push(`GRAM ${ft.node}@${t ?? '?'} "${ft.text}"`);
    }
```

## 2. Work out what the reader knows on the chapter's day

**Session.** The days of all earlier units are counted, then this day's index (0-based) plus 1. For example, u01 has 10 days and u02 has 9, so u03 day 0 is session 20 and u03 day 4 is session 24. The gate works this out too (`chapterAt`), and that number is the one that counts.

The reader knows:
- **Grammar and patterns**: every `focus` node on any day up to this session. If a node is scheduled in no unit, it is known from its graph `priority`.
- **Chunks**: every chunk up to this session, but **only as whole phrases**. If a sentence uses a chunk's words in a different way, the chunk does not cover them.
- **Words**: every lexeme whose unit day, or else `priority`, is ≤ the session. Function words (articles, pronouns, prepositions, *no*, *sí*, *y*, *pero*, *muy*, *mucho*, *gracias*…) all have priority 1. The grammar can still make them illegal, though. See the traps below.

**What the gate actually enforces**
- **legality**: every grammar node, pattern and graph lexeme the tagger finds in the text or in a gloss must be taught by this session, unless it falls inside a chunk that is already taught. **An unknown word that is in the graph cannot be glossed past this check.** Its gloss entry fails legality as well.

```ts
import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { tagSentence, splitSentences, lemmatize } from '/Users/Matthew/Fluidez/app/src/engine/tagger';
import { loadCurriculum } from '/Users/Matthew/Fluidez/app/tools/gate/load';
const cur = loadCurriculum('/Users/Matthew/Fluidez/app');
let at: number, text: string, gloss: string[] = [];
if (process.argv[2].endsWith('.json')) {
  const c = JSON.parse(readFileSync(process.argv[2], 'utf8'));
  at = cur.chapterAt.get(c.id)!; text = c.text; gloss = c.gloss.map((g: any) => g.es.toLowerCase());
} else { at = Number(process.argv[2]); text = process.argv[3]; }
const glossed = new Set<string>();
for (const g of gloss) for (const w of g.split(/[^a-záéíóúñü]+/).filter(Boolean)) { glossed.add(w); const l = lemmatize(w); if (l) glossed.add(l.lemma); }
let words = 0, unk = 0, unG = 0;
for (const s of splitSentences(text)) {
  const r = tagSentence(s, cur.tagOpts);
  words += r.tokens.filter((w) => !w.punct && w.pos !== 'propn' && w.pos !== 'num').length;
  const spans = r.features.filter((x) => x.key.startsWith('chunk.') && (cur.taughtAt.get(x.node!) ?? 1e9) <= at).map((x) => x.span);
  const inChunk = (sp: [number, number]) => spans.some(([a, b]) => sp[0] >= a && sp[1] <= b);
  const out: string[] = [];
  for (const ft of r.features) {
    if (ft.node?.startsWith('l:')) {
      const t = cur.taughtAt.get(ft.node);
      if (t !== undefined && t <= at) continue;
      unk++; const g = glossed.has(ft.node.slice(2)) || glossed.has(ft.text.toLowerCase()); if (!g) unG++;
      out.push(`${ft.text}=${ft.node}@${t ?? '?'}${g ? '(gl)' : ''}`);
    } else if (ft.node && !ft.key.startsWith('chunk.')) {
      const t = cur.taughtAt.get(ft.node);
      if ((t === undefined || t > at) && !inChunk(ft.span) && cur.graphIds.has(ft.node)) out.push(`GRAM ${ft.node}@${t ?? '?'} "${ft.text}"`);
    }
  }
  console.log(s, out.length ? '\n    ' + out.join('  ') : '');
}
console.log(`session ${at}: words ${words}, unknown ${unk} (${(100 * unk / words).toFixed(1)}%), unglossed ${unG} (${(100 * unG / words).toFixed(1)}%)`);
```

- `GRAM g:x@N` is a legality error. Rewrite the sentence.
- `word=l:x@N`, where N is greater than the session, is a legality error too, because the lexeme is in the graph. Replace the word.
- `word=l:x@?` means the word is not in the graph. It counts toward reading coverage, so gloss it or cut it.

## 2. Work out what the reader knows on the chapter's day

**Session.** The days of all earlier units are counted, then this day's index (0-based) plus 1. For example, u01 has 10 days and u02 has 9, so u03 day 0 is session 20 and u03 day 4 is session 24. The gate works this out too (`chapterAt`), and that number is the one that counts.

The reader knows:
- **Grammar and patterns**: every `focus` node on any day up to this session. If a node is scheduled in no unit, it is known from its graph `priority`.
- **Chunks**: every chunk up to this session, but **only as whole phrases**. If a sentence uses a chunk's words in a different way, the chunk does not cover them.
- **Words**: every lexeme whose unit day, or else `priority`, is ≤ the session. Function words (articles, pronouns, prepositions, *no*, *sí*, *y*, *pero*, *muy*, *mucho*, *gracias*…) all have priority 1. The grammar can still make them illegal, though. See the traps below.

List the known nouns, verbs and adjectives before you write anything. Early on the list is tiny: at session 11 the reader does not know *hoy*, *casa*, *mañana*, *hora*, *abrir*, *mesa* or *carta*. Write the story with the words you have; don't write it first and translate it afterwards.

**What the gate actually enforces**
- **legality**: every grammar node, pattern and graph lexeme the tagger finds in the text or in a gloss must be taught by this session, unless it falls inside a chunk that is already taught. **An unknown word that is in the graph cannot be glossed past this check.** Its gloss entry fails legality as well.
- **reading**: at most 2% of words unknown and unglossed, and at most 5% unknown in all. Names (tagged propn) and numerals are not counted as words. Words inside chunks still count: *Me llamo* is read as `l:llamarse` (session 72), *¿has estado?* as `l:estar`, *me gusta* as `l:gustar`.
- So **you can only gloss words that are not in the graph** (*loro*, *pacto*, *tango*, *hostel*), or phrases that are legal anyway. A gloss is also a good way to give the meaning of a whole known-word phrase: `{"es": "Soy nieto de Rosa", "en": "I'm Rosa's grandson"}`.
- **dupe**: a sentence, including its `Name:` label, that exactly matches any sentence in the corpus is an error, and that includes the bank. Running catchphrases have to vary: *¡De una!* → *Hernando y Simón: ¡De una!*
- **accent**: every `?` and `!` needs its `¿` and `¡`, **English lines too**. English lines must not contain questions or exclamations.

**Known tagger traps (as of u01–u03)**
- At the start of a sentence, or straight after a `Name:` label, *Don* is read as `l:don`, *La* as an article and *Nombre* as a command. Put *Don Hernando* and *La Esquina de Rosa* mid-sentence.
- A one-word *¿Nombre?* or *¿Apellido?* is read as a verb. Use them in a full clause: *Tomás es nombre. Herrera es apellido.*
- *nada* can be read as *nadar*, *apuesta* as *apostar* and *silencio* as *silenciar*. Choose another word.
- Articles are illegal before session 6. So are possessives (*mi*, *su*) before 44, *muy* and *mucho* as quantifiers before 63, demonstratives (*este*, *esa*, *esto*) before 59, feminine adjective agreement (*contenta*, *colombiana*) before 40, question words outside chunks before 16, *por*/*para* before 164, *si* clauses before 154 and infinitive complements (*quiero comprar*) before 72.
- *¡Vamos!*, *vamos a + verb* and *hay que / tengo que + verb* may not match their chunks. Check them before you use them.
- English words the tagger treats as Spanish lexemes, such as *we*, *to*, *and*, *is* and *okay*, count as unknown words.

```ts
import { tagSentence, splitSentences, lemmatize } from '/Users/Matthew/Fluidez/app/src/engine/tagger';
import { loadCurriculum } from '/Users/Matthew/Fluidez/app/tools/gate/load';
```

## 2. Work out what the reader knows on the chapter's day

**Session.** The days of all earlier units are counted, then this day's index (0-based) plus 1. For example, u01 has 10 days and u02 has 9, so u03 day 0 is session 20 and u03 day 4 is session 24. The gate works this out too (`chapterAt`), and that number is the one that counts.

The reader knows:
- **Grammar and patterns**: every `focus` node on any day up to this session. If a node is scheduled in no unit, it is known from its graph `priority`.
- **Chunks**: every chunk up to this session, but **only as whole phrases**. If a sentence uses a chunk's words in a different way, the chunk does not cover them.
- **Words**: every lexeme whose unit day, or else `priority`, is ≤ the session. Function words (articles, pronouns, prepositions, *no*, *sí*, *y*, *pero*, *muy*, *mucho*, *gracias*…) all have priority 1. The grammar can still make them illegal, though. See the traps below.

List the known nouns, verbs and adjectives before you write anything. Early on the list is tiny: at session 11 the reader does not know *hoy*, *casa*, *mañana*, *hora*, *abrir*, *mesa* or *carta*. Write the story with the words you have; don't write it first and translate it afterwards.

**What the gate actually enforces**
- **legality**: every grammar node, pattern and graph lexeme the tagger finds in the text or in a gloss must be taught by this session, unless it falls inside a chunk that is already taught. **An unknown word that is in the graph cannot be glossed past this check.** Its gloss entry fails legality as well.
- **reading**: at most 2% of words unknown and unglossed, and at most 5% unknown in all. Names (tagged propn) and numerals are not counted as words. Words inside chunks still count: *Me llamo* is read as `l:llamarse` (session 72), *¿has estado?* as `l:estar`, *me gusta* as `l:gustar`.
- So **you can only gloss words that are not in the graph** (*loro*, *pacto*, *tango*, *hostel*), or phrases that are legal anyway. A gloss is also a good way to give the meaning of a whole known-word phrase: `{"es": "Soy nieto de Rosa", "en": "I'm Rosa's grandson"}`.
- **dupe**: a sentence, including its `Name:` label, that exactly matches any sentence in the corpus is an error, and that includes the bank. Running catchphrases have to vary: *¡De una!* → *Hernando y Simón: ¡De una!*
- **accent**: every `?` and `!` needs its `¿` and `¡`, **English lines too**. English lines must not contain questions or exclamations.

**Known tagger traps (as of u01–u03)**
- At the start of a sentence, or straight after a `Name:` label, *Don* is read as `l:don`, *La* as an article and *Nombre* as a command. Put *Don Hernando* and *La Esquina de Rosa* mid-sentence.
- A one-word *¿Nombre?* or *¿Apellido?* is read as a verb. Use them in a full clause: *Tomás es nombre. Herrera es apellido.*
- *nada* can be read as *nadar*, *apuesta* as *apostar* and *silencio* as *silenciar*. Choose another word.
- Articles are illegal before session 6. So are possessives (*mi*, *su*) before 44, *muy* and *mucho* as quantifiers before 63, demonstratives (*este*, *esa*, *esto*) before 59, feminine adjective agreement (*contenta*, *colombiana*) before 40, question words outside chunks before 16, *por*/*para* before 164, *si* clauses before 154 and infinitive complements (*quiero comprar*) before 72.

```ts

import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { tagSentence, splitSentences, lemmatize } from '/Users/Matthew/Fluidez/app/src/engine/tagger';
import { loadCurriculum } from '/Users/Matthew/Fluidez/app/tools/gate/load';
const cur = loadCurriculum('/Users/Matthew/Fluidez/app');
let at: number, text: string, gloss: string[] = [];
if (process.argv[2].endsWith('.json')) {
  const c = JSON.parse(readFileSync(process.argv[2], 'utf8'));
  at = cur.chapterAt.get(c.id)!; text = c.text; gloss = c.gloss.map((g: any) => g.es.toLowerCase());
} else { at = Number(process.argv[2]); text = process.argv[3]; }
const glossed = new Set<string>();
for (const g of gloss) for (const w of g.split(/[^a-záéíóúñü]+/).filter(Boolean)) { glossed.add(w); const l = lemmatize(w); if (l) glossed.add(l.lemma); }
let words = 0, unk = 0, unG = 0;
for (const s of splitSentences(text)) {
  const r = tagSentence(s, cur.tagOpts);
  words += r.tokens.filter((w) => !w.punct && w.pos !== 'propn' && w.pos !== 'num').length;
  const spans = r.features.filter((x) => x.key.startsWith('chunk.') && (cur.taughtAt.get(x.node!) ?? 1e9) <= at).map((x) => x.span);
  const inChunk = (sp: [number, number]) => spans.some(([a, b]) => sp[0] >= a && sp[1] <= b);
  const out: string[] = [];
  for (const ft of r.features) {
    if (ft.node?.startsWith('l:')) {
      const t = cur.taughtAt.get(ft.node);
      if (t !== undefined && t <= at) continue;
      unk++; const g = glossed.has(ft.node.slice(2)) || glossed.has(ft.text.toLowerCase()); if (!g) unG++;
      out.push(`${ft.text}=${ft.node}@${t ?? '?'}${g ? '(gl)' : ''}`);
    } else if (ft.node && !ft.key.startsWith('chunk.')) {
      const t = cur.taughtAt.get(ft.node);
      if ((t === undefined || t > at) && !inChunk(ft.span) && cur.graphIds.has(ft.node)) out.push(`GRAM ${ft.node}@${t ?? '?'} "${ft.text}"`);
    }
  }
  console.log(s, out.length ? '\n    ' + out.join('  ') : '');
}
console.log(`session ${at}: words ${words}, unknown ${unk} (${(100 * unk / words).toFixed(1)}%), unglossed ${unG} (${(100 * unG / words).toFixed(1)}%)`);
```

- `GRAM g:x@N` is a legality error. Rewrite the sentence.
- `word=l:x@N`, where N is greater than the session, is a legality error too, because the lexeme is in the graph. Replace the word.
- `word=l:x@?` means the word is not in the graph. It counts toward reading coverage, so gloss it or cut it.
- Paste a whole batch of candidate sentences at once to learn what a session allows before you draft.

**What the gate actually enforces**

- **dupe**: a sentence, including its `Name:` label, that exactly matches any sentence in the corpus is an error, and that includes the bank. Running catchphrases have to vary: *¡De una!* → *Hernando y Simón: ¡De una!*

## 5. Coverage probe (save it in your scratchpad as `cov.ts`)

```ts
// npx tsx cov.ts <session> "<text>"   |   npx tsx cov.ts content/story/chNNN.json
import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { tagSentence, splitSentences, lemmatize } from '/Users/Matthew/Fluidez/app/src/engine/tagger';
import { loadCurriculum } from '/Users/Matthew/Fluidez/app/tools/gate/load';
const cur = loadCurriculum('/Users/Matthew/Fluidez/app');
let at: number, text: string, gloss: string[] = [];
if (process.argv[2].endsWith('.json')) {
  const c = JSON.parse(readFileSync(process.argv[2], 'utf8'));
  at = cur.chapterAt.get(c.id)!; text = c.text; gloss = c.gloss.map((g: any) => g.es.toLowerCase());
} else { at = Number(process.argv[2]); text = process.argv[3]; }
const glossed = new Set<string>();
for (const g of gloss) for (const w of g.split(/[^a-záéíóúñü]+/).filter(Boolean)) { glossed.add(w); const l = lemmatize(w); if (l) glossed.add(l.lemma); }
let words = 0, unk = 0, unG = 0;
for (const s of splitSentences(text)) {
  const r = tagSentence(s, cur.tagOpts);
  words += r.tokens.filter((w) => !w.punct && w.pos !== 'propn' && w.pos !== 'num').length;
  const spans = r.features.filter((x) => x.key.startsWith('chunk.') && (cur.taughtAt.get(x.node!) ?? 1e9) <= at).map((x) => x.span);
  const inChunk = (sp: [number, number]) => spans.some(([a, b]) => sp[0] >= a && sp[1] <= b);
  const out: string[] = [];
  for (const ft of r.features) {
    if (ft.node?.startsWith('l:')) {
      const t = cur.taughtAt.get(ft.node);
      if (t !== undefined && t <= at) continue;
      unk++; const g = glossed.has(ft.node.slice(2)) || glossed.has(ft.text.toLowerCase()); if (!g) unG++;
      out.push(`${ft.text}=${ft.node}@${t ?? '?'}${g ? '(gl)' : ''}`);
    } else if (ft.node && !ft.key.startsWith('chunk.')) {
      const t = cur.taughtAt.get(ft.node);
      if ((t === undefined || t > at) && !inChunk(ft.span) && cur.graphIds.has(ft.node)) out.push(`GRAM ${ft.node}@${t ?? '?'} "${ft.text}"`);
    }
  }
  console.log(s, out.length ? '\n    ' + out.join('  ') : '');
}
console.log(`session ${at}: words ${words}, unknown ${unk} (${(100 * unk / words).toFixed(1)}%), unglossed ${unG} (${(100 * unG / words).toFixed(1)}%)`);
```

How to read its output:
- `GRAM g:x@N` is a legality error. Rewrite the sentence.
- `word=l:x@N`, where N is greater than the session, is a legality error too, because the lexeme is in the graph. Replace the word.
- `word=l:x@?` means the word is not in the graph. It counts toward reading coverage, so gloss it or cut it.
- Paste a whole batch of candidate sentences at once to learn what a session allows before you draft.

## 2. What a script may use

A script's legality position is **the session on which its node is first in a day's `focus`**, and the node itself is allowed. So the u01 *ser* script (session 1) has no articles, no *-ar* verbs and about 130 words, mostly function words; the *-ar* script (session 8) has everything up to day 8. ## 3. Anatomy (all required unless marked)

- **`hook`**: `line` = the human reason, in one or two plain sentences ("The first thing anyone in Bogotá will want to know is who you are…"); `es`/`en` = a line the learner would actually say, ideally from the story's world.
- **`examples`** (≥ 3; aim for 6): before the rule. Vary person, polarity, statement/question. `en` pins person and formality.
- **`rule`** (≤ 150 words, ~90 s reading): plain English, no jargon, built on the examples. Contrast with English and say what disappears or changes. Lists of forms are fine as short lines.
- **`smallPrint`**: the technical term, once ("Teachers call this…").
- **`soundTip`** (optional): only where a new sound matters. Describe it against English ("rhymes with *boy*", "like the *tt* in an American *better*"). Never assume audio.
- **`readAndPick`** (≥ 8): structured input. Spanish `es`, 2–3 English `options`, `answer` index. It must be **solvable only by noticing the form** (ending, article, mark, word order): options differ in exactly the thing being taught (*Somos de Cali* → we / they / I). Vary the position of the right answer.
- **`yourTurn`** (≥ 6): a ladder: **choose** (gap + two forms, type the whole sentence) → **type** (English prompt, Spanish answer) → **transform** (make it negative / plural / about *we* / polite). Each has `why`: one plain sentence, the reason in the learner's terms. `accept` lists real alternatives (word-order variants, *Me llamo* / *Soy*); every answer and accept must be typeable and legal.
- **`pitfalls`** (3–5): predicted English-speaker mistakes, `wrong` → `right` + `why` in one sentence ("Almost. *Es* tells you what something is…").
- **`personal`**: a closing prompt to say something true about yourself with the new form.

**Patterns** (`p:` nodes) are shorter but complete: 4–6 examples, a rule of ≤ 100 words, 8 readAndPick, 6–7 yourTurn, 3 pitfalls. Their readAndPick usually contrasts the pattern with what an English speaker would write (*Soy mesero* = a waiter vs *Soy el mesero* = the waiter).

- Prompts pin person, number and formality whenever the answer depends on it ("to a friend", "you all", "a woman speaking").

## 1. Read first, in full

1. `tools/burn/brief.md`. These rules are binding.
2. `docs/unit-map.md`: the cast, the stakes and the story beat for every unit. Also look at the next two units, so you know where this week is heading.
3. `content/units/<unit>.json` for each unit: its `storyArc`, and for each day its `chapter`, `focus`, `chunks` and `lexemes`.
4. **Every earlier chapter** in `content/story/`, in order. Note the running jokes, what each character knows, the last hook (your first chapter has to pay it off) and the openings already used. Never reuse an opening or a plot device.

## 2. Work out what the reader knows on the chapter's day

**Session.** The days of all earlier units are counted, then this day's index (0-based) plus 1. For example, u01 has 10 days and u02 has 9, so u03 day 0 is session 20 and u03 day 4 is session 24. The gate works this out too (`chapterAt`), and that number is the one that counts.

The reader knows:
- **Grammar and patterns**: every `focus` node on any day up to this session. If a node is scheduled in no unit, it is known from its graph `priority`.
- **Chunks**: every chunk up to this session, but **only as whole phrases**. If a sentence uses a chunk's words in a different way, the chunk does not cover them.
- **Words**: every lexeme whose unit day, or else `priority`, is ≤ the session. Function words (articles, pronouns, prepositions, *no*, *sí*, *y*, *pero*, *muy*, *mucho*, *gracias*…) all have priority 1. The grammar can still make them illegal, though. See the traps below.

List the known nouns, verbs and adjectives before you write anything. Early on the list is tiny: at session 11 the reader does not know *hoy*, *casa*, *mañana*, *hora*, *abrir*, *mesa* or *carta*. Write the story with the words you have; don't write it first and translate it afterwards.

**What the gate actually enforces**
- **legality**: every grammar node, pattern and graph lexeme the tagger finds in the text or in a gloss must be taught by this session, unless it falls inside a chunk that is already taught. **An unknown word that is in the graph cannot be glossed past this check.** Its gloss entry fails legality as well.
- **reading**: at most 2% of words unknown and unglossed, and at most 5% unknown in all. Names (tagged propn) and numerals are not counted as words. Words inside chunks still count: *Me llamo* is read as `l:llamarse` (session 72), *¿has estado?* as `l:estar`, *me gusta* as `l:gustar`.
- So **you can only gloss words that are not in the graph** (*loro*, *pacto*, *tango*, *hostel*), or phrases that are legal anyway. A gloss is also a good way to give the meaning of a whole known-word phrase: `{"es": "Soy nieto de Rosa", "en": "I'm Rosa's grandson"}`.
- **dupe**: a sentence, including its `Name:` label, that exactly matches any sentence in the corpus is an error, and that includes the bank. Running catchphrases have to vary: *¡De una!* → *Hernando y Simón: ¡De una!*
- **accent**: every `?` and `!` needs its `¿` and `¡`, **English lines too**. English lines must not contain questions or exclamations.

**Known tagger traps (as of u01–u03)**
- At the start of a sentence, or straight after a `Name:` label, *Don* is read as `l:don`, *La* as an article and *Nombre* as a command. Put *Don Hernando* and *La Esquina de Rosa* mid-sentence.
- A one-word *¿Nombre?* or *¿Apellido?* is read as a verb. Use them in a full clause: *Tomás es nombre. Herrera es apellido.*
- *nada* can be read as *nadar*, *apuesta* as *apostar* and *silencio* as *silenciar*. Choose another word.
- Articles are illegal before session 6. So are possessives (*mi*, *su*) before 44, *muy* and *mucho* as quantifiers before 63, demonstratives (*este*, *esa*, *esto*) before 59, feminine adjective agreement (*contenta*, *colombiana*) before 40, question words outside chunks before 16, *por*/*para* before 164, *si* clauses before 154 and infinitive complements (*quiero comprar*) before 72.
- *¡Vamos!*, *vamos a + verb* and *hay que / tengo que + verb* may not match their chunks. Check them before you use them.
- English words the tagger treats as Spanish lexemes, such as *we*, *to*, *and*, *is* and *okay*, count as unknown words.

```ts
import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { tagSentence, splitSentences, lemmatize } from '/Users/Matthew/Fluidez/app/src/engine/tagger';
import { loadCurriculum } from '/Users/Matthew/Fluidez/app/tools/gate/load';
const cur = loadCurriculum('/Users/Matthew/Fluidez/app');
let at: number, text: string, gloss: string[] = [];
if (process.argv[2].endsWith('.json')) {
  const c = JSON.parse(readFileSync(process.argv[2], 'utf8'));
  at = cur.chapterAt.get(c.id)!; text = c.text; gloss = c.gloss.map((g: any) => g.es.toLowerCase());
} else { at = Number(process.argv[2]); text = process.argv[3]; }
const glossed = new Set<string>();
for (const g of gloss) for (const w of g.split(/[^a-záéíóúñü]+/).filter(Boolean)) { glossed.add(w); const l = lemmatize(w); if (l) glossed.add(l.lemma); }
let words = 0, unk = 0, unG = 0;
for (const s of splitSentences(text)) {
  const r = tagSentence(s, cur.tagOpts);
  words += r.tokens.filter((w) => !w.punct && w.pos !== 'propn' && w.pos !== 'num').length;
  const spans = r.features.filter((x) => x.key.startsWith('chunk.') && (cur.taughtAt.get(x.node!) ?? 1e9) <= at).map((x) => x.span);
  const inChunk = (sp: [number, number]) => spans.some(([a, b]) => sp[0] >= a && sp[1] <= b);
  const out: string[] = [];
  for (const ft of r.features) {
    if (ft.node?.startsWith('l:')) {
      const t = cur.taughtAt.get(ft.node);
      if (t !== undefined && t <= at) continue;
      unk++; const g = glossed.has(ft.node.slice(2)) || glossed.has(ft.text.toLowerCase()); if (!g) unG++;
      out.push(`${ft.text}=${ft.node}@${t ?? '?'}${g ? '(gl)' : ''}`);
    } else if (ft.node && !ft.key.startsWith('chunk.')) {
      const t = cur.taughtAt.get(ft.node);
      if ((t === undefined || t > at) && !inChunk(ft.span) && cur.graphIds.has(ft.node)) out.push(`GRAM ${ft.node}@${t ?? '?'} "${ft.text}"`);
    }
  }
  console.log(s, out.length ? '\n    ' + out.join('  ') : '');
}
console.log(`session ${at}: words ${words}, unknown ${unk} (${(100 * unk / words).toFixed(1)}%), unglossed ${unG} (${(100 * unG / words).toFixed(1)}%)`);
```

- `word=l:x@?` means the word is not in the graph. It counts toward reading coverage, so gloss it or cut it.

```ts
import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { tagSentence, splitSentences, lemmatize } from '/Users/Matthew/Fluidez/app/src/engine/tagger';
import { loadCurriculum } from '/Users/Matthew/Fluidez/app/tools/gate/load';
const cur = loadCurriculum('/Users/Matthew/Fluidez/app');
let at: number, text: string, gloss: string[] = [];
if (process.argv[2].endsWith('.json')) {
  const c = JSON.parse(readFileSync(process.argv[2], 'utf8'));
  at = cur.chapterAt.get(c.id)!; text = c.text; gloss = c.gloss.map((g: any) => g.es.toLowerCase());
} else { at = Number(process.argv[2]); text = process.argv[3]; }
const glossed = new Set<string>();
for (const g of gloss) for (const w of g.split(/[^a-záéíóúñü]+/).filter(Boolean)) { glossed.add(w); const l = lemmatize(w); if (l) glossed.add(l.lemma); }
let words = 0, unk = 0, unG = 0;
for (const s of splitSentences(text)) {
  const r = tagSentence(s, cur.tagOpts);
  words += r.tokens.filter((w) => !w.punct && w.pos !== 'propn' && w.pos !== 'num').length;
  const spans = r.features.filter((x) => x.key.startsWith('chunk.') && (cur.taughtAt.get(x.node!) ?? 1e9) <= at).map((x) => x.span);
  const inChunk = (sp: [number, number]) => spans.some(([a, b]) => sp[0] >= a && sp[1] <= b);
  const out: string[] = [];
  for (const ft of r.features) {
    if (ft.node?.startsWith('l:')) {
      const t = cur.taughtAt.get(ft.node);
      if (t !== undefined && t <= at) continue;
      unk++; const g = glossed.has(ft.node.slice(2)) || glossed.has(ft.text.toLowerCase()); if (!g) unG++;
      out.push(`${ft.text}=${ft.node}@${t ?? '?'}${g ? '(gl)' : ''}`);
    } else if (ft.node && !ft.key.startsWith('chunk.')) {
      const t = cur.taughtAt.get(ft.node);
      if ((t === undefined || t > at) && !inChunk(ft.span) && cur.graphIds.has(ft.node)) out.push(`GRAM ${ft.node}@${t ?? '?'} "${ft.text}"`);
    }
  }
  console.log(s, out.length ? '\n    ' + out.join('  ') : '');
}
console.log(`session ${at}: words ${words}, unknown ${unk} (${(100 * unk / words).toFixed(1)}%), unglossed ${unG} (${(100 * unG / words).toFixed(1)}%)`);
```

How to read its output:
- `GRAM g:x@N` is a legality error. Rewrite the sentence.
- `word=l:x@N`, where N is greater than the session, is a legality error too, because the lexeme is in the graph. Replace the word.
- `word=l:x@?` means the word is not in the graph. It counts toward reading coverage, so gloss it or cut it.
- Paste a whole batch of candidate sentences at once to learn what a session allows before you draft.
